{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the final stretch of the top line, from the crossing down to the lower tail tip. That is the join where the two lines meet, and it was the last piece needed to complete the fish. Once it was in, the start domino traced through all 112 standing dominoes, nose to both tail tips. I also stocked the shared bin with a full 40-domino batch early, so builders could keep laying without stopping to fetch.

Execution: I fetched the bin batch in one trip, which is the efficient way to carry. I inspected the nose split and the tail crossing closely, three times before the tail work and once after, to confirm the chain was connected. I laid the tail stretch in short, careful batches, stood one domino back up near the lower tail tip, and then confirmed the crossing was clean. After that I kept my hands off so the finished work wouldn't get bumped.

Collaboration: I told the table what I was checking and when. I offered to take the last stretch of the top line before it was needed, and when we agreed on it I asked people to keep clear of the tail so we didn't bump each other. I answered Leo's request to check the crossing and reported back that it was clean. I also backed the group's decision to stop building and let the fish ride.

Leadership: I saw that the tail crossing was the riskiest spot and put my free hands there instead of adding more to the picture. I took ownership of that stretch and finished it. I also pushed for a clean, hands-off finish so the connected run stayed intact for the push.", "my_share_percent": 20}
